It's a minarchist approach that adds in layers of transparency, accountability, and citizen oversight. Firstly, we would abolish all taxes, and the sole source of guaranteed income the government would have would be tariffs, as it was when the country was first founded. Day to day legislation would be up to the states, and the purpose of the federal government would largely be providing for external defense, facilitating inter state commerce, and adjudicating between states for the most part. Again, as the founders set up.

Here's where the "open source" bit comes in. Every government agent and elected official shall be made to wear a live streaming, publicly viewable body cam at all times. They can take it off for restroom breaks and when they're home. They're also required to wear gps tracking ankle bracelets at all times, and all official communications including phone calls, txts, emails, etc will be viewable on a public server. Harsh and very imposing, sure. But it will bring the highest level of transparency and accountability, and only those who are truly honest and upstanding will subject themselves to such surveillance.

The states will be restricted in what they can do as well. Their primary role will be protecting the natural rights of their citizens, and providing police, courts, and infrastructure. Anything above the bare minimum will be voluntary and crowd funded. If people want socialized health care for example, the state can set up a public fund through voluntary contributions like a gofundme. If you don't want to participate, you don't have to pay for it. In this way, states can fund things like welfare, public schools, state militias, etc. They'd have to collect some form of taxes or tariffs to provide infrastructure and a police force, though. This could be accomplished by state tariffs or property taxes, or a number of things. It would be left up to the state, and any compulsory tax like that would be strictly limited to the aforementioned bare minimum services.

Additionally, ranked choice voting would be used to protect against political parties getting too powerful, and all laws would be subject to a public veto, as well as a public reauthorization vote every so often. Say once a decade or something like that. In addition to the aforementioned public surveillance of the government, all legislative sessions will be observable to the public, made open for public questioning, and the entire text of the bill made available for a sufficient amount of time prior to the vote, after which a public veto vote shall also be held.
